transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Lucas (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Product), Daniel, Sophie, Raj, Ellen (Aurora)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Demo of Redwood Eval & Quality Monitoring. Showed prompt set management, regression alerts, A/B comparison workflow, and how Evaluate ties into Console and Optimize. Customer interested in pilot, privacy constraints (VPC/Dedicated), and integration with existing CI. Next steps and owners agreed.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - appreciate you making time. Quick intros, and then Lucas will walk through the Eval and quality monitoring flow.
[00:18] Daniel: Hey all, Daniel here, head of ML at Aurora. We're looking at how to detect regression across prompts after model updates, and also how to A/B test newer models with our freight promo copy workload.
[00:34] Sophie: Hi I'm Sophie, product; we care about user-visible regressions and automated alerts so PMs don't only find issues in dashboards after the fact.
[00:46] Lucas: Awesome. So I wanna start with a high-level: Redwood Eval organizes prompt sets as named suites, you can attach gold labels and evaluation metrics, then schedule runs on model versions. We also have regression alerts that trigger when key metrics fall beyond thresholds, and A/B comparison tooling to compare model A vs model B over the same prompt cohort.
[01:12] Raj: Quick Q - how intrusive is onboarding? We have data residency constraints and some prompts contain PII-ish customer examples.
[01:24] Maya: Good callout. For pilot we typically do two options: hosted with strict retention and RBAC, or Dedicated/private where the control plane is customer-managed and logs live in your VPC. We'll include our security pack in the follow up.
[01:38] Ellen: We need KMS/HSM support and audit logs for any data leaving our environment.
[01:44] Priya: To add, Optimize can recommend quantization and batching settings, but for eval specifically you can pin a model variant and run side-by-side comparisons.
[02:05] Lucas: Jumping into the Console - opening Eval tab now, apologies for slight lag. You'll see an examples table - groups of prompt sets: "promo_headlines_v1", "returns_flow", "fraud_detection_examples". Each prompt set has metadata like owner, labels, and expected outputs.
[02:28] Sophie: Can we upload CSVs or is there an API?
[02:34] Lucas: Both. Upload CSV via UI or push via API; we also have a Git-backed flow if you want canonical prompt sets under version control.
[02:44] Daniel: How do you handle fuzzy label matches? Our labels are not strict equality; we use paraphrase acceptance and tolerance.
[02:53] Lucas: Good question - we support multiple metric types: exact match, ROUGE, BLEU-ish, embedding similarity (cosine) with configurable thresholds, and custom scorers you can plug in. The regression alerting uses a chosen metric and looks for delta relative to baseline or control cohort.
[03:20] Sophie: And the alerts - slack? pager?
[03:25] Lucas: Yep, Slack, email, webhooks; can also create an incident in your tickets system. You can tune noise with holdout windows and required delta percentage.
[03:38] [05:00] Lucas: (screen) Demo: create a new run - pick model A (open model v2 quantized), model B (proprietary v3), and run across "promo_headlines_v1". Here you can select metrics: embedding sim > 0.8 and human-labeled quality > 0.7. After the run completes we show per-prompt diffs and a summary distribution chart.
[05:42] Sophie: Are these runs synchronous? How long do they take at scale?
[05:49] Lucas: It depends - for small suites under 5k prompts it’s near real-time on Hosted. For larger corpora we recommend batch runs on Dedicated. We also have continuous monitoring mode: it attaches to production traffic, samples by route, and runs evals periodically.
[06:10] Daniel: Sampling - does that respect data masking? We can't ship full user messages to hosted endpoints.
[06:18] Lucas: You can enable prefix seeding or anonymization at ingestion; sensitive fields can be stripped or hashed client-side before sending. On Private/Dedicated we can run everything inside your network.
[06:32] Raj: What's the uplift to cost when doing continuous monitoring?
[06:36] Priya: Cost depends on sample rate, model choices (quantized vs fp16), and whether you use hosted inference or reserved Dedicated nodes. Optimize will suggest efficient configurations - e.g., run metric scoring on cheaper embeddings model and only call full gen on edge cases.
[06:55] [10:00] Lucas: Now the A/B comparison view - side-by-side scoring, per-prompt delta heatmap, and a regression timeline that shows when a metric crossed your alert threshold. You can click a single prompt to see model outputs and label comparison.
[10:28] Daniel: Can we plug in our external human evals? We have a small panel of raters.
[10:34] Lucas: Absolutely - there's an import for human scores, and you can combine automated metrics with human labels to drive composite alerts.
[10:45] Sophie: We need to run acceptance tests post rollout. Can Redwood trigger canary rollouts based on eval results?
[10:52] Maya: Yes - Redwood's rollout integration can automatically hold or rollback a model based on failing eval checks. You can configure canary size and the pass/fail gates.
[11:05] [15:00] Lucas: Here's an example of a regression alert fired last week; the timeline shows a drop in embedding-sim across the "returns_flow" suite after a model version upgrade. You can trace which prompts drove the change, open the prompt and see token-level diffs.
[12:20] Ellen: Nice. For compliance we need exportable audit trails - who's run evals, who approved thresholds.
[12:30] Lucas: Exportable CSVs and an audit log with user IDs and timestamps are available; plus SSO/SAML mapping for roles.
[12:40] Raj: Any limitations on custom scorers? We want to run a semantic rule engine in our infra.
[12:48] Lucas: You can host scoring logic in your infra and call back via webhook, or bundle the scorer as a lightweight lambda in Redwood Private. We surface the result as a metric.
[13:10] Sophie: For A/B - how do you ensure statistical significance? Does Redwood provide power analysis?
[13:18] Lucas: We provide sample-size recommendations, p-values for key metrics and a summary that flags if the difference is likely noise. You can also set minimum effect-size thresholds.
[13:32] [20:00] Maya: Moving to the API surface quickly - endpoints for uploading prompt suites, kicking off runs, fetching per-prompt diffs, and subscribing to alerts. Also example SDK calls in Python and Node.
[13:50] Daniel: About data egress - if we run on Hosted and send masked examples, do we retain logs?
[13:58] Maya: Retention is configurable; for Hosted we have short retention options (e.g., 30 days) and strict RBAC. Dedicated/Private retains per your policies. All access is logged.
[14:12] Sophie: If we want to A/B a new base model from OpenAI or Anthropic, can Redwood orchestrate that?
[14:18] Lucas: Yep - Redwood supports a model catalog with connectors; you can define versioned model endpoints and also fallback policies.
[14:25] Daniel: What's the onboarding timeline for a pilot? We want to do a two-week pilot that runs our promo_headlines and returns_flow suites.
[14:32] Maya: For a standard pilot we usually do: Week 0 - onboarding and prompt import; Week 1 - baseline runs and configuration; Week 2 - two A/B runs and final results + recommendations. We'll scope exact SLOs in the follow-up.
[14:46] Priya: We'll also add Optimize suggestions after the baselines so you can see cost/latency tradeoffs.
[14:52] [25:00] Daniel: Any gotchas with tokenization differences across models? We saw earlier that special characters affected scoring.
[15:00] Lucas: Tokenization differences can skew exact-match metrics; we recommend using embedding-based similarity for free-form text and normalize whitespace/characters during pre-process. We support normalization rules in the eval pipeline.
[15:20] Ellen: For our CI we want an API hook to fail a PR if regression detected.
[15:26] Lucas: There's a webhook to post a pass/fail result which you can integrate as a git check. Many customers wire that into pipelines.
[15:35] Sophie: If a regression alert triggers, can we auto-run a human-in-the-loop review?
[15:40] Lucas: Yes, you can route flagged prompts to a reviewer queue, and once human approval is given Redwood can auto-approve a rollback or move forward.
[15:54] [30:00] Maya: Pricing overview - usage-based for Hosted eval runs (per-eval token/compute), reserved capacity options for Dedicated, plus an onboarding fee for Private deployments. We'll send a specimen pricing sheet.
[16:20] Raj: For Dedicated, what's the SLA on eval run latency?
[16:26] Priya: SLA depends on capacity reservations; for example reserving a small cluster yields predictable throughput and sub-second scoring on small suites. We'll include examples in the follow-up.
[16:40] Daniel: Any references or similar customers?
[16:45] Maya: We've done pilots with retail and finance customers for promo copy and document summarization. We'll anonymize and send case studies.
[16:55] [35:00] Lucas: Quick demo: create an automated regression alert - set baseline on model v1, threshold -3% on embedding-sim, alert to slack channel #ml-regressions, and set a 24 hour holdout to avoid flapping. Trigger a synthetic regression and show the alert.
[17:18] Sophie: Looks good. Can the alert include per-prompt examples in the message?
[17:22] Lucas: Yes, with a sample of the top N offending prompts and a link to full run in the console.
[17:32] Daniel: We will need to map roles - who can dismiss alerts?
[17:36] Lucas: RBAC covers that; you can restrict dismiss rights to particular groups.
[17:40] [40:00] Maya: Recap of next steps: we'll send pricing and security pack, Redwood will run a 2k prompt baseline (Lucas to run), Aurora to share canonical prompt sets and thresholds (Daniel), and schedule deep-dive next week.
[40:30] Daniel: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[40:35] Raj: Appreciate it, talk soon.
[40:38] Maya: Thanks all - we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

End of transcript.
